data.next: Not this line. E161's load-bearing claim (that the exposed population already knows) is untested but low-stakes; the prevalence measurement it names would not change the build decision. Move to a fresh population with a real, independent oracle.
data.summary: Prior-art and demand probes returned weak for a CSV coercion linter (a handful of high-vote reports; 0-to-1-star tools that already do parts of it). E161 then measured the mechanism on real files with a real engine: 1,206,342 cells through LibreOffice Calc 6.4.7.2 headless, cell-level diff against source text. 36,697 leading-zero GEOID cells damaged in the US Census 2023 Gazetteer (9.5% of that file); 0 damaging cells in 818,222 cells of analyst exports and public-body registers; 13 of 78 folklore controls damaged. csvsafe.py (200 lines, stdlib, 10 tests) reproduces the engine at precision 1.0 and recall 1.0 on two real frames and flags 36,697 TP / 0 FP / 0 FN; csvsafe write takes the census file to 0 damaging cells. Not a candidate: the frame where damage is common is machine-produced tables whose publishers already ship .xlsx. Kept unreleased at status: draft, plus the round-trip instrument the four synthetic-fixture experiments lacked.
